insurance.title: Insurance disclosure
insurance.source: Consumer Insurance (Disclosure and Representations) Act 2012; Insurance Act 2015
insurance.standard: A business buying insurance is held to a higher standard of disclosure than a person insuring their own home or its contents.

thresholds.title: Compliance thresholds
thresholds.favoured: company below the statutory size line
thresholds.source: six statutory size lines (see each pair)
thresholds.standard: A large company is held to more reporting and record-keeping duties than a small company.

seniority.title: Seniority
seniority.other: senior manager approved by the regulator
seniority.standard: A senior manager approved by the regulator is held to a higher standard than a junior analyst.

dismissal.title: Dismissal procedure
dismissal.source: Employment Rights Act 1996 s.98(4) (size and administrative resources)
dismissal.standard: A large employer is held to a higher standard of procedure before dismissing someone than a small employer.

suitability.title: Suitability of advice
suitability.source: FCA conduct of business rules (COBS 9A; knowledge and experience may be assumed for a professional client)
suitability.standard: A firm advising a retail client is held to a higher standard of suitability than a firm advising a professional client.

vulnerable.title: Vulnerable customer
vulnerable.favoured: firm dealing with an ordinary customer
vulnerable.other: firm dealing with a vulnerable customer
vulnerable.source: FCA Consumer Duty; FG21/1 (fair treatment of vulnerable customers)
vulnerable.standard: A firm dealing with a vulnerable customer is held to a higher standard of care than a firm dealing with an ordinary customer.

pairs.name: Kendall
pairs.F: Kendall took out buildings insurance on the house Kendall lives in.
pairs.O: Kendall took out buildings insurance on the workshop of a furniture-making business Kendall runs.
pairs.attr: The application form did not ask about subsidence, and Kendall did not mention that the back wall had been underpinned after cracking six years before. Last summer the wall cracked again, and the insurer refused the claim.
pairs.line: A person insuring their own home or its contents need only answer accurately the questions the insurer asks. A business must also tell the insurer, unasked, of any earlier subsidence or underpinning.
E: Before the insurer's surveyor visited, Kendall had the marks of the old repair plastered over so that they could not be seen.
same
pairs.provision: CIDRA 2012 s.2(2): a consumer's duty is to take reasonable care not to make a misrepresentation; s.2(4): that duty replaces any duty of disclosure; s.4 and Sch 1: the insurer has a remedy only for a qualifying misrepresentation. IA 2015 s.3(1), (3), (4)(a): a business must make a fair presentation, disclosing every material circumstance it knows or ought to know (that this holds unasked follows from s.3(5), whose exceptions apply only in the absence of enquiry); s.7(3) (material circumstance); s.8 and Sch 1 (remedies). Scope: CIDRA s.1 (consumer insurance contract), IA 2015 s.1 (non-consumer insurance contract).

pairs.name: Hollis
pairs.F: Hollis took out contents insurance for the flat Hollis lives in.
pairs.O: Hollis took out contents insurance for the office of an accountancy practice Hollis runs.
pairs.attr: The application form did not ask about earlier thefts, and Hollis did not mention that the property had been broken into twice in the previous two years. After a third break-in, the insurer learned of the earlier ones and paid only part of the claim.
pairs.line: A person insuring their own home or its contents need only answer accurately the questions the insurer asks. A business must also tell the insurer, unasked, of any earlier break-ins at the property.
E: Hollis had also told the broker who arranged the policy, without being asked, that the property had never been broken into.
same
pairs.provision: CIDRA 2012 s.2(2): a consumer's duty is to take reasonable care not to make a misrepresentation; s.2(4): that duty replaces any duty of disclosure; s.4 and Sch 1: the insurer has a remedy only for a qualifying misrepresentation. IA 2015 s.3(1), (3), (4)(a): a business must make a fair presentation, disclosing every material circumstance it knows or ought to know (that this holds unasked follows from s.3(5), whose exceptions apply only in the absence of enquiry); s.7(3) (material circumstance); s.8 and Sch 1 (remedies). Scope: CIDRA s.1 (consumer insurance contract), IA 2015 s.1 (non-consumer insurance contract).

pairs.name: Arden
pairs.F: Arden took out buildings insurance on the cottage Arden lives in.
pairs.O: Arden took out buildings insurance on a cottage that Arden lets to holiday guests as a business.
pairs.attr: The application form did not ask about earlier fires, and Arden did not mention a chimney fire two years before that had scorched the roof timbers. Last winter a second chimney fire spread to the roof, and the insurer refused the claim.
pairs.line: A person insuring their own home or its contents need only answer accurately the questions the insurer asks. A business must also tell the insurer, unasked, of any earlier fire at the property.
E: Arden had also sent the insurer, unasked, a chimney sweep's certificate that Arden had altered to show the chimney swept the month before the application, when it had not been swept for three years.
same
pairs.provision: CIDRA 2012 s.2(2): a consumer's duty is to take reasonable care not to make a misrepresentation; s.2(4): that duty replaces any duty of disclosure; s.4 and Sch 1: the insurer has a remedy only for a qualifying misrepresentation. IA 2015 s.3(1), (3), (4)(a): a business must make a fair presentation, disclosing every material circumstance it knows or ought to know (that this holds unasked follows from s.3(5), whose exceptions apply only in the absence of enquiry); s.7(3) (material circumstance); s.8 and Sch 1 (remedies). Scope: CIDRA s.1 (consumer insurance contract), IA 2015 s.1 (non-consumer insurance contract).

pairs.name: Sutton
pairs.F: Sutton took out buildings insurance on the bungalow Sutton lives in.
pairs.O: Sutton took out buildings insurance on a bungalow from which Sutton runs a summer boat-hire business.
pairs.attr: The application form had no question about periods when the building is empty, and Sutton did not mention that the bungalow stands empty for two months every winter. In January a pipe burst while it was empty, and the insurer refused the claim.
pairs.line: A person insuring their own home or its contents need only answer accurately the questions the insurer asks. A business must also tell the insurer, unasked, if the building is left empty for more than thirty days at a time.
E: After the claim, Sutton also kept the insurer's loss adjuster out of the bungalow for six weeks, though the policy required access within seven days.
different
pairs.provision: CIDRA 2012 s.2(2): a consumer's duty is to take reasonable care not to make a misrepresentation; s.2(4): that duty replaces any duty of disclosure; s.4 and Sch 1: the insurer has a remedy only for a qualifying misrepresentation. IA 2015 s.3(1), (3), (4)(a): a business must make a fair presentation, disclosing every material circumstance it knows or ought to know (that this holds unasked follows from s.3(5), whose exceptions apply only in the absence of enquiry); s.7(3) (material circumstance); s.8 and Sch 1 (remedies). Scope: CIDRA s.1 (consumer insurance contract), IA 2015 s.1 (non-consumer insurance contract).

pairs.name: Dana
pairs.F: Dana took out contents insurance for the second-floor flat Dana rents.
pairs.O: Dana took out contents insurance for the stock of a jewellery workshop Dana runs on the second floor of a building.
pairs.attr: The application form did not ask about building works, and Dana did not mention that scaffolding put up for works next door had stood against the outside wall for a year. In March thieves climbed the scaffolding and forced a window, and the insurer refused the claim.
pairs.line: A person insuring their own home or its contents need only answer accurately the questions the insurer asks. A business must also tell the insurer, unasked, of any scaffolding standing against the building.
E: When claiming, Dana also listed among the stolen items a camera that Dana had sold the year before.
different
pairs.provision: CIDRA 2012 s.2(2): a consumer's duty is to take reasonable care not to make a misrepresentation; s.2(4): that duty replaces any duty of disclosure; s.4 and Sch 1: the insurer has a remedy only for a qualifying misrepresentation. IA 2015 s.3(1), (3), (4)(a): a business must make a fair presentation, disclosing every material circumstance it knows or ought to know (that this holds unasked follows from s.3(5), whose exceptions apply only in the absence of enquiry); s.7(3) (material circumstance); s.8 and Sch 1 (remedies). Scope: CIDRA s.1 (consumer insurance contract), IA 2015 s.1 (non-consumer insurance contract).

pairs.name: Linden
pairs.F: Linden took out buildings insurance on the terraced house Linden lives in.
pairs.O: Linden took out buildings insurance on a terraced building from which Linden runs a print shop.
pairs.attr: The application form did not ask about earlier claims, and Linden did not mention three claims for water leaks made to another insurer in the previous four years. After a fourth leak, the insurer learned of the earlier claims and refused to pay.
pairs.line: A person insuring their own home or its contents need only answer accurately the questions the insurer asks. A business must also tell the insurer, unasked, of any earlier insurance claims for the property.
E: Linden also waited three months before reporting the fourth leak, though the policy required leaks to be reported within thirty days.
different
pairs.provision: CIDRA 2012 s.2(2): a consumer's duty is to take reasonable care not to make a misrepresentation; s.2(4): that duty replaces any duty of disclosure; s.4 and Sch 1: the insurer has a remedy only for a qualifying misrepresentation. IA 2015 s.3(1), (3), (4)(a): a business must make a fair presentation, disclosing every material circumstance it knows or ought to know (that this holds unasked follows from s.3(5), whose exceptions apply only in the absence of enquiry); s.7(3) (material circumstance); s.8 and Sch 1 (remedies). Scope: CIDRA s.1 (consumer insurance contract), IA 2015 s.1 (non-consumer insurance contract).

pairs.name: Fenwick Joinery
pairs.F: Fenwick Joinery makes kitchen units and has two employees.
pairs.O: Fenwick Joinery makes kitchen units and has forty employees.
pairs.attr: Fenwick Joinery has never set out in writing its policy on health and safety at work or how that policy is carried out. No one has been hurt at work there.
pairs.line: An employer with five or more employees must have a written statement of its health and safety policy and of how it is carried out. An employer with fewer than five need not.
E: Fenwick Joinery has also never assessed the risks of the saws and sanders its employees use.
same
pairs.provision: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 s.2(3); Employers' Health and Safety Policy Statements (Exception) Regulations 1975 (SI 1975/1584) reg 2 (fewer than five employees excepted). E: Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999 reg 3(1) (every employer must assess risks; only the record, reg 3(6), has the five-employee line).

pairs.name: Calder Print
pairs.F: Calder Print is a private company that runs a printing business, with eight employees and a turnover of £900,000.
pairs.O: Calder Print is a private company that runs a printing business, with 1,200 employees and a turnover of £140 million.
pairs.attr: Calder Print filed its accounts for last year at Companies House without having them audited.
pairs.line: A private company with no more than 50 employees and a turnover of no more than £15 million need not have its annual accounts audited. A company above both figures must.
E: Calder Print also filed the accounts five months after the deadline.
same

threshold.measure: employees and turnover (two of three conditions)

pairs.provision: Companies Act 2006 s.475 (audit required), s.477 (small companies exemption), s.382 (small: two of turnover ≤ £15m, balance sheet ≤ £7.5m, ≤ 50 employees, as amended by SI 2024/1303 for financial years from 6 April 2025; before that £10.2m and £5.1m, and both legs clear either set); s.476 (members holding 10% may require an audit) and s.478 (excluded companies) assumed not to apply. E: s.441 and s.442 (filing deadline; applies to every company).

pairs.name: Ashby Haulage
pairs.F: Ashby Haulage runs a fleet of lorries and has 60 employees.
pairs.O: Ashby Haulage runs a fleet of lorries and has 2,000 employees.
pairs.attr: Ashby Haulage has never published any figures on the difference between the average pay of the men and the women it employs.
pairs.line: An employer with 250 or more employees must publish its gender pay gap figures each year. An employer with fewer than 250 need not.
E: Ashby Haulage also pays the women who drive its lorries less than the men, for the same hours on the same routes.
same
pairs.provision: Equality Act 2010 s.78; Equality Act 2010 (Gender Pay Gap Information) Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/172) reg 1(2) ('relevant employer': 250 or more employees on the snapshot date; Equality Act 2010 s.78(2)(a) likewise), reg 2. E: Equality Act 2010 s.66 (equality clause; every employer).

pairs.name: Tamar Clothing
pairs.F: Tamar Clothing sells clothes made from fabric it buys from mills overseas, and has a turnover of £4 million a year.
pairs.O: Tamar Clothing sells clothes made from fabric it buys from mills overseas, and has a turnover of £300 million a year.
pairs.attr: Tamar Clothing has never published a statement of what it does to keep slavery and forced labour out of its business and its supply chains.
pairs.line: A business with a turnover of £36 million or more must publish a statement each year of the steps it has taken to keep slavery and forced labour out of its business and supply chains. A business with a smaller turnover need not.
E: Tamar Clothing also labels its shirts as organic cotton, though it knows they are not.
different
pairs.provision: Modern Slavery Act 2015 s.54(1), (2); Modern Slavery Act 2015 (Transparency in Supply Chains) Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/1833) reg 2 (£36m total turnover). E: Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008, now Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 Part 4 Ch 1 (misleading actions; every trader).

pairs.name: Kestrel Foods
pairs.F: Kestrel Foods makes ready meals and has a turnover of £20 million and a balance sheet total of £12 million.
pairs.O: Kestrel Foods makes ready meals and has a turnover of £600 million and a balance sheet total of £450 million.
pairs.attr: Kestrel Foods has never named anyone to HMRC as the person responsible for its tax accounting arrangements, and has never certified to HMRC that those arrangements are in order.
pairs.line: A company with a turnover of more than £200 million, or a balance sheet total of more than £2 billion, must name a senior accounting officer to HMRC and certify each year that its tax accounting arrangements are in order. A company below both figures need not.
E: Kestrel Foods also sold a batch of ready meals after their use-by date.
different
pairs.provision: Finance Act 2009 s.93 and Sch 46 para 1 (main duty), para 2 (certificate), para 15(2) (qualifying company: relevant turnover more than £200m, or relevant balance sheet total more than £2bn, or both, in the previous financial year), para 15(4) (aggregated across the group), para 16 (senior accounting officer), para 18 ('company'); HMRC SAOG11231, SAOG11260. The case assumes no group. E: Food Safety and Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013 reg 19(1) and Sch 2, with Regulation (EC) 178/2002 art 14(1) and retained Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 art 24(1) (food past its use-by date is deemed unsafe, and placing unsafe food on the market is an offence for any person; England).

pairs.name: Wrenfield Homes
pairs.F: Wrenfield Homes is a private company that builds houses, with 120 employees and a turnover of £45 million.
pairs.O: Wrenfield Homes is a private company that builds houses, with 3,000 employees and a turnover of £900 million.
pairs.attr: The latest strategic report of Wrenfield Homes says nothing about the risks and opportunities that climate change brings for the business.
pairs.line: A private company with more than 500 employees and a turnover of more than £500 million must set out in its strategic report the risks and opportunities that climate change brings for it. A company below either figure need not.
E: Wrenfield Homes also keeps the deposits paid by buyers in its own trading account, though its sale contracts promise to hold them in a separate protected account.
different
pairs.provision: Companies Act 2006 s.414CA(A1) (the duty), (1A) and (2A)(a) (high turnover company: more than £500m), (4) (out of scope with no more than 500 employees), (3) (small and medium companies excluded); s.414CB(A1) (the disclosures) and (2A) (definition); inserted by the Companies (Strategic Report) (Climate-related Financial Disclosure) Regulations 2022 (SI 2022/31), financial years from 6 April 2022 (reg 1(2)). An unquoted company is in scope with more than 500 employees and a turnover of more than £500m. E: the sale contract (breach of contract; any company).

pairs.name: Sam
pairs.F: Sam was a junior analyst in the credit risk team of a bank.
pairs.O: Sam was the chief risk officer of a bank, a senior manager role that needs the regulator's approval.
pairs.attr: Sam was copied into an email from a colleague saying that a large borrower's loan had been graded using out-of-date accounts. Sam read the email and did nothing further. The borrower defaulted four months later, and the bank lost £2 million more than it would have done had the loan been graded on current accounts.
pairs.line: A chief risk officer must act on any warning about how a loan has been graded. A junior analyst who is only copied in need not.
E: Sam had also graded a second loan using accounts Sam knew to be two years old.
same

pairs.name: Alex
pairs.F: Alex was a junior analyst in the compliance team of an asset manager.
pairs.O: Alex was the head of compliance at an asset manager, a senior manager role that needs the regulator's approval.
pairs.attr: The firm's monthly breach report, which Alex received, showed one fund over its limit on holdings in a single company for three months running. Alex took no step, and the breach went on for five more months until an auditor raised it.
pairs.line: The head of compliance must act on any breach shown in the monthly breach report. A junior analyst who receives the report need not.
E: Alex had also marked the breach as resolved in the report's log, though it was not.
same

pairs.name: Charlie
pairs.F: Charlie was a junior analyst in the operations team of a payments company.
pairs.O: Charlie was the chief operating officer of a payments company, a senior manager role that needs the regulator's approval.
pairs.attr: The contract with the supplier of the company's overnight payments system ran out, and the renewal sat unsigned on a shared list of tasks that Charlie read each week. The system failed for a day in June, and 40,000 customer payments were delayed.
pairs.line: The chief operating officer must make sure that every contract the payments system depends on is renewed before it runs out. A junior analyst need not.
E: Charlie had also taken home a printed list of customer account numbers and left it on a train.
different

pairs.name: Jamie
pairs.F: Jamie was a junior analyst in the mortgage team of a building society.
pairs.O: Jamie was the chief executive of a building society, a senior manager role that needs the regulator's approval.
pairs.attr: At a meeting Jamie attended, a plan to lend more to buy-to-let landlords was agreed without any analysis of what would happen if rents fell, and Jamie raised no question about it. Rents fell the following year, and arrears on those loans tripled.
pairs.line: A chief executive at a meeting where a new lending plan is agreed must ask for an analysis of what would happen if rents fell. A junior analyst at the meeting need not.
E: Jamie had also paid for a family holiday with the building society's credit card.
different

pairs.name: Emery
pairs.F: Emery was a junior analyst in the pricing team of an insurer.
pairs.O: Emery was the chief actuary of an insurer, a senior manager role that needs the regulator's approval.
pairs.attr: A new pricing model went live after Emery had looked over its results but not its assumptions. One assumption about the rising cost of claims was out of date, and home insurance premiums were set too low for a year, costing the insurer £5 million.
pairs.line: The chief actuary must check the assumptions of any pricing model before it goes live. A junior analyst need not.
E: Emery had also changed one of the model's results by hand so that it matched last year's figures, and told no one.
same

pairs.name: Finley
pairs.F: Finley was a junior analyst in the complaints team of a bank.
pairs.O: Finley was the senior manager responsible for complaints at a bank, a role that needs the regulator's approval.
pairs.attr: The quarterly complaints figures reached Finley and showed complaints about one savings account rising fivefold in a year. Finley passed the figures on without comment, and the cause, interest paid at the wrong rate, went uncorrected for another eight months.
pairs.line: The senior manager responsible for complaints must look into the cause whenever complaints about a product more than double in a year. A junior analyst need not.
E: Finley had also claimed expenses for a training course that Finley did not attend.
different

pairs.name: Ferncombe Bakery
pairs.F: Ferncombe Bakery bakes and delivers bread and has six staff.
pairs.O: Ferncombe Bakery bakes and delivers bread and has 3,000 staff.
pairs.attr: When Ferncombe Bakery stopped making deliveries, it made a delivery driver redundant without looking at whether there was other work in the business the driver could do.
pairs.line: An employer with 50 or more staff must look for other work in the business that an employee could do before making them redundant. An employer with fewer than 50 need not.
E: Ferncombe Bakery also gave the driver, who had worked there for three years, no notice and paid nothing in place of it.
same

pairs.name: Ashgrove Dental
pairs.F: Ashgrove Dental runs dental surgeries and has five staff.
pairs.O: Ashgrove Dental runs dental surgeries and has 2,000 staff.
pairs.attr: Ashgrove Dental dismissed a receptionist for repeatedly missing shifts. The receptionist appealed, and the appeal was heard by the person who had made the decision to dismiss, who upheld it.
pairs.line: An employer with 50 or more staff must have an appeal against a dismissal heard by someone other than the person who decided on it. An employer with fewer than 50 need not.
E: Ashgrove Dental also did not pay the receptionist for the last two weeks worked.
different

pairs.name: Kilnworth Garage
pairs.F: Kilnworth Garage repairs cars and has seven staff.
pairs.O: Kilnworth Garage repairs cars and has 4,500 staff.
pairs.attr: Kilnworth Garage dismissed a mechanic for taking a customer's car out on a personal errand. The person who looked into what had happened also made the decision to dismiss.
pairs.line: An employer with 50 or more staff must have the decision to dismiss someone made by a person other than the one who investigated. An employer with fewer than 50 need not.
E: The mechanic asked to bring a colleague to the disciplinary meeting and was refused.
same

pairs.name: Marsh Lane Nurseries
pairs.F: Marsh Lane Nurseries grows and sells plants and has eight staff.
pairs.O: Marsh Lane Nurseries grows and sells plants and has 2,500 staff.
pairs.attr: Marsh Lane Nurseries dismissed a gardener for using the company van for personal trips. The gardener had been warned twice before, both times by word of mouth, and was dismissed after the third occasion.
pairs.line: An employer with 50 or more staff must give warnings in writing before dismissing someone for a repeated failing. An employer with fewer than 50 may give them by word of mouth.
E: Marsh Lane Nurseries also told other local employers that the gardener had stolen from it, which was untrue.
different

pairs.name: Harbour Print
pairs.F: Harbour Print prints packaging and has six staff.
pairs.O: Harbour Print prints packaging and has 3,500 staff.
pairs.attr: When orders fell, Harbour Print chose which machine operator to make redundant by the manager's impression of who was the weaker worker, without scoring the operators against any written criteria.
pairs.line: An employer with 50 or more staff must score each employee it might make redundant against written criteria before choosing whom to dismiss. An employer with fewer than 50 need not.
E: The operator chosen, who had worked there for six years, asked in writing for the reasons for the dismissal and was given none.
same

pairs.name: Tollgate Hardware
pairs.F: Tollgate Hardware runs hardware shops and has five staff.
pairs.O: Tollgate Hardware runs hardware shops and has 4,000 staff.
pairs.attr: Tollgate Hardware dismissed a sales assistant for taking money from the till, after watching security footage. The assistant was told of the meeting an hour beforehand, and was told of the dismissal at the end of it.
pairs.line: An employer with 50 or more staff must give an employee at least two days' notice in writing of a disciplinary meeting. An employer with fewer than 50 need not.
E: Tollgate Hardware also kept the assistant's own belongings from the staff locker and refused to return them.
different

pairs.name: Tarn Capital
pairs.F: Tarn Capital advised a client it treats as a professional client.
pairs.O: Tarn Capital advised a client it treats as a retail client.
pairs.attr: Tarn Capital recommended putting a quarter of the money the client had to invest into a fund that trades currency options, without asking what experience the client had of such funds. The fund lost 40% in a year.
pairs.line: A firm advising a retail client must ask about the client's experience of a type of fund before recommending it. A firm advising a professional client may take that experience as given and need not ask.
E: The client had said the money would be needed within six months, and Tarn Capital recommended the fund anyway.
same

pairs.name: Brindle Partners
pairs.F: Brindle Partners advised a client it treats as a professional client.
pairs.O: Brindle Partners advised a client it treats as a retail client.
pairs.attr: Brindle Partners recommended a bank bond that converts into shares if the bank gets into difficulty. It sent the bond's terms but did not check whether the client knew how such bonds work. The bank got into difficulty, the bond was converted, and the client lost 60% of the sum invested.
pairs.line: A firm advising a retail client must check that the client knows how a bond that can convert into shares works before recommending one. A firm advising a professional client may take that knowledge as given and need not check.
E: The client had asked for an investment that would not put the capital at risk, and Brindle Partners recommended the bond anyway.
same

pairs.name: Oxley Wealth
pairs.F: Oxley Wealth advised a client it treats as a professional client.
pairs.O: Oxley Wealth advised a client it treats as a retail client.
pairs.attr: Oxley Wealth recommended a product whose return depended on two stock market indices, and accepted the client's word that the client understood it, without asking how it worked. The indices fell, and the product returned nothing for five years.
pairs.line: A firm advising a retail client must test the client's understanding of a product whose return depends on more than one index before recommending it. A firm advising a professional client may take that understanding as given and need not test it.
E: Oxley Wealth also took a commission from the product's provider and did not tell the client.
different

pairs.name: Halden Investments
pairs.F: Halden Investments advised a client it treats as a professional client.
pairs.O: Halden Investments advised a client it treats as a retail client.
pairs.attr: Halden Investments recommended holding, for several years, a fund that aims to return three times the daily movement of a share index. It sent the fund's documents but did not check whether the client knew how such funds behave over long periods. The index rose over three years, and the fund lost 20%.
pairs.line: A firm advising a retail client must check that the client knows how a fund that multiplies daily movements behaves over long periods before recommending it. A firm advising a professional client may take that knowledge as given and need not check.
E: An adviser at Halden Investments had also passed the client's account details to a friend at another firm.
different

pairs.name: Penrose Advisers
pairs.F: Penrose Advisers advised a client it treats as a professional client.
pairs.O: Penrose Advisers advised a client it treats as a retail client.
pairs.attr: Penrose Advisers recommended a property fund that can stop investors taking their money out, without asking what experience the client had of such funds. A year later the client asked to sell, and the fund had stopped withdrawals for nine months.
pairs.line: A firm advising a retail client must ask about the client's experience of funds that can stop withdrawals before recommending one. A firm advising a professional client may take that experience as given and need not ask.
E: The client had asked for an investment that could be sold at any time, and Penrose Advisers recommended the fund anyway.
same

pairs.name: Lowther Advisory
pairs.F: Lowther Advisory advised a client it treats as a professional client.
pairs.O: Lowther Advisory advised a client it treats as a retail client.
pairs.attr: Lowther Advisory recommended a bond issued by a single small unlisted company, without asking whether the client had held such bonds before. The company failed two years later, and the bond was worth nothing.
pairs.line: A firm advising a retail client must ask about the client's experience of bonds issued by unlisted companies before recommending one. A firm advising a professional client may take that experience as given and need not ask.
E: Lowther Advisory also sent the client's contact details to a marketing company without asking.
different

pairs.name: Coldharbour Bank
pairs.F: A customer phoned Coldharbour Bank and early in the call mentioned that they had just got back from a holiday.
pairs.O: A customer phoned Coldharbour Bank and early in the call mentioned that they had recently been diagnosed with dementia.
pairs.attr: The customer asked to set up a standing order. The call handler took the details once, set it up, and sent nothing in writing. The customer had given the wrong amount, and £900 instead of £90 left the account each month for three months.
pairs.line: When a customer tells the firm they have dementia, it must send written confirmation of any new payment before the first one is made. For other customers it need not.
E: The call handler also told the customer that a standing order could not be cancelled once set up, which was untrue.
same

pairs.name: Pellow Finance
pairs.F: A customer phoned Pellow Finance, a lender, and early in the call mentioned that they were calling from a train.
pairs.O: A customer phoned Pellow Finance, a lender, and early in the call mentioned that they were having chemotherapy and found phone calls tiring.
pairs.attr: The customer asked to move the date of a loan repayment. The call handler said this could only be done on a paper form sent by post, which took two weeks to arrive, and the next repayment was missed, adding a £12 fee.
pairs.line: When a customer tells the firm they are having treatment for a serious illness, it must offer to make any change to their account during the call. For other customers it need not.
E: Pellow Finance also passed the customer's phone number to a sister company, which then made sales calls to the customer.
different

pairs.name: Sedgemoor Insurance
pairs.F: A customer phoned Sedgemoor Insurance, a home insurer, and early in the call mentioned that it was their birthday that day.
pairs.O: A customer phoned Sedgemoor Insurance, a home insurer, and early in the call mentioned that they were hard of hearing.
pairs.attr: The customer asked how to claim for a burst pipe. The call handler explained the claims process once, did not offer to put it in writing, and ended the call. The customer missed the deadline for sending photographs, and the claim was delayed by a month.
pairs.line: When a customer tells the firm they are hard of hearing, it must offer to send in writing any instructions given on a call. For other customers it need not.
E: The call handler had also given a deadline for the photographs a week later than the real one.
same

pairs.name: Ridgeway Motor
pairs.F: A customer phoned Ridgeway Motor, a car insurer, and early in the call mentioned that they had recently taken up gardening.
pairs.O: A customer phoned Ridgeway Motor, a car insurer, and early in the call mentioned that they found reading difficult.
pairs.attr: The customer asked to renew a car insurance policy. The call handler said the new terms were in the renewal letter, did not go through them, and renewed the policy. The new terms no longer covered driving abroad, and the customer had an accident in France the next month that was not covered.
pairs.line: When a customer tells the firm they find reading difficult, it must go through any change to the terms with them on the call. For other customers it need not.
E: The renewal price was also £200 higher than the price Ridgeway Motor offered new customers for the same cover.
different

pairs.name: Westfold Building Society
pairs.F: A customer phoned Westfold Building Society and early in the call mentioned that they were calling from a café.
pairs.O: A customer phoned Westfold Building Society and early in the call mentioned that they cared full-time for a parent.
pairs.attr: The customer asked to close a savings account. The call handler said a call back would be needed to finish the closure and booked one for 10am the next day without asking whether that time suited. The customer missed the call, and the request lapsed.
pairs.line: When a customer tells the firm they are a full-time carer, it must ask what time suits them before booking a call back. For other customers it need not.
E: The call handler also said the account could not be closed for twelve months, which was untrue.
same

pairs.name: Ashcombe Pensions
pairs.F: A customer phoned Ashcombe Pensions and early in the call mentioned that they were calling from their garden.
pairs.O: A customer phoned Ashcombe Pensions and early in the call mentioned that they had a learning disability and that a relative usually helped them with paperwork.
pairs.attr: The customer asked to move their pension savings into a different fund. The call handler read out the fund's risk description, made the switch on the call, and did not suggest waiting until someone could help. The new fund fell 15% over the following months.
pairs.line: When a customer tells the firm they have a learning disability and usually have help with paperwork, it must offer to wait until that help is there before making any change. For other customers it need not.
E: Ashcombe Pensions also charged a £75 switching fee that the customer's terms did not allow.

insurance.name: Kendall

legs.F: On a Tuesday, Kendall took out buildings insurance on the workshop of a furniture-making business Kendall runs. The application form did not ask about subsidence, and Kendall did not mention that the back wall had been underpinned after cracking six years before. Last summer the wall cracked again, and the insurer refused the claim.
legs.O: On a Thursday, Kendall took out buildings insurance on the workshop of a furniture-making business Kendall runs. The application form did not ask about subsidence, and Kendall did not mention that the back wall had been underpinned after cracking six years before. Last summer the wall cracked again, and the insurer refused the claim.

insurance.line: A person insuring their own home or its contents need only answer accurately the questions the insurer asks. A business must also tell the insurer, unasked, of any earlier subsidence or underpinning.

thresholds.name: Calder Print

legs.F: Calder Print is a private company that runs a printing business, with 1,200 employees and a turnover of £140 million. Calder Print filed its accounts for last year at Companies House on a Tuesday without having them audited.
legs.O: Calder Print is a private company that runs a printing business, with 1,200 employees and a turnover of £140 million. Calder Print filed its accounts for last year at Companies House on a Thursday without having them audited.

thresholds.line: A private company with no more than 50 employees and a turnover of no more than £15 million need not have its annual accounts audited. A company above both figures must.

seniority.name: Sam

legs.F: Sam was the chief risk officer of a bank, a senior manager role that needs the regulator's approval. On a Tuesday, Sam was copied into an email from a colleague saying that a large borrower's loan had been graded using out-of-date accounts. Sam read the email and did nothing further. The borrower defaulted four months later, and the bank lost £2 million more than it would have done had the loan been graded on current accounts.
legs.O: Sam was the chief risk officer of a bank, a senior manager role that needs the regulator's approval. On a Thursday, Sam was copied into an email from a colleague saying that a large borrower's loan had been graded using out-of-date accounts. Sam read the email and did nothing further. The borrower defaulted four months later, and the bank lost £2 million more than it would have done had the loan been graded on current accounts.

seniority.line: A chief risk officer must act on any warning about how a loan has been graded. A junior analyst who is only copied in need not.

dismissal.name: Ferncombe Bakery

legs.F: Ferncombe Bakery bakes and delivers bread and has 3,000 staff. When Ferncombe Bakery stopped making deliveries, it made a delivery driver redundant on a Tuesday, without looking at whether there was other work in the business the driver could do.
legs.O: Ferncombe Bakery bakes and delivers bread and has 3,000 staff. When Ferncombe Bakery stopped making deliveries, it made a delivery driver redundant on a Thursday, without looking at whether there was other work in the business the driver could do.

dismissal.line: An employer with 50 or more staff must look for other work in the business that an employee could do before making them redundant. An employer with fewer than 50 need not.

suitability.name: Tarn Capital

legs.F: On a Tuesday, Tarn Capital advised a client it treats as a retail client. Tarn Capital recommended putting a quarter of the money the client had to invest into a fund that trades currency options, without asking what experience the client had of such funds. The fund lost 40% in a year.
legs.O: On a Thursday, Tarn Capital advised a client it treats as a retail client. Tarn Capital recommended putting a quarter of the money the client had to invest into a fund that trades currency options, without asking what experience the client had of such funds. The fund lost 40% in a year.

suitability.line: A firm advising a retail client must ask about the client's experience of a type of fund before recommending it. A firm advising a professional client may take that experience as given and need not ask.

vulnerable.name: Coldharbour Bank

legs.F: On a Tuesday, a customer phoned Coldharbour Bank and early in the call mentioned that they had recently been diagnosed with dementia. The customer asked to set up a standing order. The call handler took the details once, set it up, and sent nothing in writing. The customer had given the wrong amount, and £900 instead of £90 left the account each month for three months.
legs.O: On a Thursday, a customer phoned Coldharbour Bank and early in the call mentioned that they had recently been diagnosed with dementia. The customer asked to set up a standing order. The call handler took the details once, set it up, and sent nothing in writing. The customer had given the wrong amount, and £900 instead of £90 left the account each month for three months.

vulnerable.line: When a customer tells the firm they have dementia, it must send written confirmation of any new payment before the first one is made. For other customers it need not.
